summary.tldr: Requires warning labels on alcoholic beverages and sets out what those labels must say.
what_it_does: Requires any beverage with 1.1% alcohol by volume or more to be sold in a package with a warning label in the prescribed form and manner.
Requires the label to warn consumers about the health risks of alcohol consumption.
Requires the label to show the volume that counts as a standard drink, the number of standard drinks in the package, and the number that should not be exceeded to avoid significant health risks.
Requires the label to include a Department message about the direct causal link between alcohol consumption and fatal cancers.
Brings the changes into force one year after royal assent.
summary.background: It adds a new section to the Food and Drugs Act.
